newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia reports two oil finds for 1996.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia reports two oil finds for 1996.

text.p: Tunisia has made two oil finds during 1996 in the southern region, a senior energy official said on Tuesday.

The first find is at the Oued Zar field, where the the first production tests were up to 2,500 barrels per day (bpd), Rachid Gribaa, Deputy Director general of the state-run Entreprise Tunisienne d'Activites Petrolieres (ETAP) told an oil forum in the Tunisian city of Sfax.
The second is at the Chorbane field. Gribaa said: "There was a good flow of oil...it promises too much," he said without giving a figure.
The Oued Zar field is being explored by Italy's Agip SpA in a joint venture with ETAP.
Chorbane field is operated by Kuwaiti's Kufpec in association with ETAP.
Tunisia produced 4.231 million tonnes of crude oil in 1995, down slightly from 4.364 million tonnes in 1994.
More than 140 firms, mostly foreign, are attending the three-day Sfax exhibition in this southern Tunsian city.
